description_en: Cibāhāḥ Nani is a branch of the Cikã Bahī, which is located towards its west. The Nani is a small, primarily residential courtyard containing a two-storied god house (dyaḥchẽ) with two adjoiningphalcāsto its south. This god house has two storeys, and is the main monument of the courtyard. The rest of the buildings surrounding the courtyard are private houses. A small, eastern-facing statue of Gaṇeśa has been attached to the wall of the house south of the god house. Similarly, an image of Mahākāla is attached to the wall of the house west of the god house. An image of Bhairava is attached to the wall of a house to the west of the courtyard (which is in line with the temple). The courtyard has stone flooring and the space remains in a state of neglect despite its rich heritage and cultural importance.The god house is home to a rectangular sanctum with a slightly projected main entrance. This entrance is at the western side, and is flanked by two stone lions. Atoraṇashowing images of Buddha, Nāmasaṅgīti and Lokeśvara has been fixed on top of the carved door. The sanctum in turn houses statues of Buddha, Nāmasaṅgīti and Lokeśvara, all of which have been placed on top of stone pedestals. However, the image of Nāmasaṅgīti has been stolen. After the theft, an iron fence was installed in front of the entrance for protection.As is standard for Newar temples, the ground floor is separated from the first floor by a five layer timber cornice band. The first floor has a carved door in its principal elevation, and its window is flanked by oval-shaped painted surfaces. The other facades of the temple have blank walls. The middle wall of the second floor of the god house contains a carved window flanked by two wall paintings of Sthānaka Lokeśvaras. Four struts with images of Buddhist deities support the tiled roof of the house. Some years ago, the southern side of the worn roof was partially repaired with zinc sheets. However, other parts of the roof are also badly damaged, with some tiles having fallen down. In some sections, the rafters and battens are exposed to the elements, making them at risk for rot. Thepura, once placed at the centre of the roof, is now lying broken, and the pinnacle which once stood on top of this is no longer there.Aphucāhas been attached to the temple on its southern side. Importantly, it indicates the presence of the stone statues of Sarasvati, Gaṇeśa and Laxmi at its rear wall. Aśikharakūṭacaityasits at the centre of the courtyard. Thiscaityais peculiar, as it has a pair of guardian animals on every side but the northern one. It seems as though there was once a statue there but that it has perhaps been lost or stolen.It is interesting to note that of all the houses around the court, the northern house is the only Newar style house. Upon closer appraisal, one can see that it has a wide plinth that has been edged in stone. These stones have holes that posts once slotted into, which indicates that the stone pieces must have been brought from some place nearby. It could also be speculated that this courtyard once had a colonnaded ground floor and that these stones therefore belonged to the structure all along.A stone inscription near to the entrance of the sanctum informs its readers that this monastic building was constructed by a member of Cikã Bahī Saṅgha in NS 991 (CE 1871) and that the founder had endowed the site withguṭhīlands to fund its ritual worship. Nowadays, however, theguṭhīno longer owns this land. Theguṭhīmembers have therefore begun collecting money from one another so that they can continue to hold the annualvarṣavardhana pūjāand other rituals. Theguṭhīmembers of the monastic buildings once performed the daily worship in turn, however this tradition no longer exists.
description_ne: चिकं बहीबाट पश्चिममा दिशामा अवस्थित यो चिबाहाः ननि चिकं बहीकै शाखा विहार हो । सानो चोकको पूर्वतिर दुईतले द्यःछेँ र द्यःछेँसँगै जोडिएको फल्चा रहेको छ । द्यःछेँ बाहेक अन्य तीन दिशाहरूमा आवासीय घरहरू छन् । चोकको केन्द्रमा एउटा शिखरकूट चैत्य छ । दक्षिणतिर फल्चाले छोएको द्यःछेँको अन्य तीनतर्फी भागलाई कुनै संरचनाले छोएको छैन । द्यःछेँबाट दक्षिणपट्टि रहेको घरको भित्तामा गणेशको सानो मूर्ति र पश्चिममा पर्ने घरको भित्तामा महाकालको सानो मूर्ति टाँसिएको देख्न सकिन्छ । द्यःछेँको ढोका दायाँ–बायाँ एकजोडा सिंहमूर्ति स्थापित छ । कलात्मक काष्ठ ढोकामाथि तोरण छ जसको केन्द्रमा त्रिरत्नका मूर्तिहरू कुँदिएका छन् । द्यःछेँको गर्भमा त्रिरत्नको प्रतीक बुद्ध, नामसंगीति र षडक्षरी लोकेश्वरको मूर्ति ढुङ्गामाथि राखिएका थिए तर यी तीन मूर्तिमध्ये नामसंगीतिको मूर्ति भने चोरी भैसक्यो । चोरीको घटनापश्चात् सुरक्षार्थ ढोकाबाहिर फलामे बारले घेरिएको छ । द्यःछेँको दोस्रो तल्लाको बीच भागमा एक कलात्मक काष्ठ झ्याल रहेको छ । उक्त झ्यालको दायाँ–बायाँ स्थानक लोकेश्वरको भित्तेचित्र कोरिएको छ । द्यःछेँको झिँगटीको छानोलाई थाम्न देवताका मूर्ति कुँदिएका ४ वटा टुँडाल राखिएका छन् । झिँगटीको छानो जीर्ण भएकाले पश्चिमी भागमा केही वर्ष पहिला जस्तापाताले छाइएको छ । छानोको बीच भागमा रहेको पुर जीर्ण भई भत्किसकेको अवस्था छ भने पुरको धातुको गजूर पनि चोरी भैसक्यो ।द्यःछेँको ढोकासँगै एउटा अभिलेख उभ्याइएको छ जसअनुसार यस विहारको निर्माण नेसं ९९१ मा चिकंबही संघका एक सदस्यपरिवारबाट भएको थियो । उक्त शिलालेखमा नवनिर्मित विहारको पूजाआजा सम्पन्न गर्न जग्गा दान गरी गुठीको व्यवस्था गरेको कुरा उल्लेख छ । गुठीका जग्गाहरू पनि गुठीको स्वामित्वमा नरहेपछि गुठीयारहरूबाटै खर्च उठाई विहारको वर्षवर्धन एवं अन्य वार्षिक कर्म सम्पन्न हुँदैआएको छ ।विगतमा विहारका गुठी खलकहरूले क्रमिक रूपमा नित्यपूजाको जिम्मेवारी लिई पूजा चलाउँदै आए पनि हाल सो क्रम रोकिएको अवस्था छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Navarāja Bhāro and Suryarāja Bhāro constructed theśikharakūṭacaityaand bestowed theguṭhīwith lands to fund the annual rituals.
Bhājuvīra, Mānavīra and Siddhimāna constructed thebāhāḥand donated lands for the establishment of theguthī,so that the group could manage the daily and annual ritual worships.
